He became king in 2013 when his father abdicated for health reasons, and his eldest daughter, Princess Elisabeth, is now first in line to succeed him — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium: King of the Belgians since 2013.
Known in Hebrew as 'praises,' this anthology of 150 religious hymns is divided into five sections each closing with a doxology — which book of the Bible is it?
Psalms: Book of sacred songs in the Hebrew Bible.
This ten-headed demon king of Lanka abducted the hero's wife in an ancient Hindu epic and is now burned in effigy every year during a festival marking his defeat — who is he?
Ravana: Primary antagonist in the Hindu epic Ramayana.
Nicknamed 'Fighting Bob,' this Wisconsin progressive served as governor and senator before running for president in 1924 on a party he made himself — who is it?
Robert M. La Follette: American lawyer and politician (1855–1925)
Nicknamed Iran's 'hanging judge,' this cleric headed the country's revolutionary court from 1979 to 1981 and ordered the destruction of a former shah's mausoleum — who was he?
Sadegh Khalkhali: Iranian cleric and politician (1926–2003)
This Roman general's victory over Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC earned him an honorific epithet referencing the continent he conquered — who was he?
Scipio Africanus: Roman general and politician (236/235 – c. 183 BC)
Known by the honorific Bangabandhu, this founding president of Bangladesh was assassinated in a 1975 coup after leading the country since 1972 — who is he?
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman: Bangladeshi revolutionary and statesman (1920–1975)
After finding fame as Tulsi in India's most-watched soap opera, this actress-turned-politician joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2003 and later held roles in India's Union Cabinet — who is she?
Smriti Irani: Indian actress and politician (born 1976)
He founded a Korean new religious movement known for mass 'Blessing' wedding ceremonies, and also launched an international news company behind The Washington Times — who was this messiah claimant?
Sun Myung Moon: Korean religious leader (1920–2012)
This Aztec god of the night sky, hurricanes, and conflict had the jaguar as his animal double, and his main festival involved ritual human sacrifice — who is he?
Tezcatlipoca: Aztec deity of darkness and violence.
A vocal champion of the crypto industry in Congress, this Minnesota Republican has served as House majority whip since 2023 after narrowly losing a gubernatorial bid in 2010. Who is he?
Born in the Ukrainian SSR, this politician served as Russia's ambassador to Malta and Greece before becoming Governor of Saint Petersburg and eventually chairing the Federation Council — who is she?

Highly regarded as a military strategist, this Vietnamese general led communist forces to victory across the decades-long Indochina wars, while also serving as minister of defense and deputy prime minister. Who is he?
Võ Nguyên Giáp: Vietnamese general and communist politician (1911–2013)

A paratrooper with Easy Company's 101st Airborne in World War II, this veteran co-wrote a memoir with fellow soldier 'Babe' Heffron and was portrayed by Frank John Hughes in a famed HBO miniseries — who is he?
Serving as head of state under Lenin's new government until his death in 1919, this Bolshevik organizer of the October Revolution also chaired the party's Secretariat — who was he?
Founder of the Pakistan People's Party, this barrister-statesman served as both president and prime minister of Pakistan before his 1977 overthrow and 1979 execution — who was he?
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto: 4th President and 9th Prime Minister of Pakistan (1928–1979)
Who among these was born first?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (born 1847) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
TeX (published 1978) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Ernest Lawrence is a physicist. A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
Pick the chemist from these four.
What is the atomic number of Helium?
Helium: Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
In what year was John Forbes Nash Jr. born?
John Forbes Nash Jr.: Nash and fellow game theorists John Harsanyi and Reinhard Selten were awarded the 1994 Nobel Prize in Economics.
In what year was Gabe Newell born?
Gabe Newell: Gabe Logan Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
In what year was Carl Friedrich Gauss born?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: Gauss was director of the Göttingen Observatory in Germany and professor of astronomy from 1807 until his death in 1855.
In what year did Maria Montessori die?
Maria Montessori: At an early age, Montessori enrolled in classes at an all-boys technical school, with hopes of becoming an engineer.
In what year did Hedy Lamarr die?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 – January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.
In what year was HIV/AIDS discovered?
HIV/AIDS: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system.
In what year was COVID-19 discovered?
COVID-19: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2.
Mannitol: Pfizer. Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication.
In which country did the Junkers Ju 87 take place?
Junkers Ju 87: Germany. The Junkers Ju 87, popularly known as the "Stuka", is a German dive bomber and ground-attack aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Tellurium?
Tellurium: Franz-Joseph Müller von Reichenstein. Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Who is credited with discovering Einsteinium?
Einsteinium: Albert Ghiorso. Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
Who is credited with discovering Neon?
Neon: William Ramsay. Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.
Affecting about 1 in 30,000 newborns, this inherited condition — also called rod monochromacy — brings color blindness, poor acuity, and a curious day-blindness. What is it?
Achromatopsia is a medical syndrome that exhibits symptoms relating to five conditions, most notably monochromacy.
With one stable isotope and the rank of 12th-most-abundant element in the universe, this lightweight metal carries atomic number 13 — what is it?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
This scientific discipline bridges biology and sociology, studying human behavior, cultures, societies, and languages across time. What field is it?

Anthropology is the scientific study of humanity that crosses biology and sociology, concerned with human behavior, human biology, cultures, societies, and linguistics, in both the present and past, including archaic humans.
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
Accepted by the American Kennel Club in 1893, this small, compact dog breed with a short tail and erect ears originated in the United States — name the breed?
Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Sporting one pair of legs per body segment, this venomous arthropod always has an odd number of leg pairs — anywhere from 15 to 191 — what is it?

Centipede (from Neo-Latin centi- 'hundred' and Latin pes, pedis 'foot') are predatory arthropods belonging to the class Chilopoda of the subphylum Myriapoda, an arthropod group which includes millipedes and other multi-legged animals.
This small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa is often called a 'cat' in its common nickname, despite not actually being a cat at all — what is it?
Civet is a small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa, especially the tropical forests.

Forming colonies of thousands of genetically identical, sac-like polyps, these marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons behind the world's tropical reefs — name them?
Coral are colonial marine invertebrates within the subphylum Anthozoa of the phylum Cnidaria.
Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered photoelasticity and an angle that bears his name — and also improved the stereoscope. Who was he?
David Brewster (11 December 1781 - 10 February 1868) was a Scottish scientist, inventor, author, and academic administrator.
Charles Darwin spent years experimenting on these mucilage-coated plants, first proving that plants could be carnivorous — which genus of nearly 200 "sundew" species is it?
Drosera is commonly known as the sundews, is one of the largest genera of carnivorous plants, with at least 194 species.
This discipline systematically applies natural science and mathematics to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft under real-world constraints. What field is it?
Engineering is the practice of systematically applying natural science and mathematics to design and improve systems, devices, or processes that solve problems under constraints.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.
This 1984 period drama imagines a bitter rivalry between an 18th-century Vienna composer and his jealous rival, who resolves to ruin the genius's career. What film is it?
Glyphosate (IUPAC name: N-(phosphonomethyl)glycine) is a broad-spectrum systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, feeds only on blood, and has legs too short and stumpy to jump or even walk well on a flat surface — what is it?
Head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) is an obligate ectoparasite of humans.
While first described from Virginia, this genus of flowering shrubs reaches its greatest diversity in East Asia, and some species climb up to 30 metres by scaling trees. What plant is it?
Hydrangea (or) is a genus of more than 70 species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
This German polymath wrote The Sorrows of Young Werther and essays on botany, anatomy, and color theory—he's the most influential writer in the German language. Who was he?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 - 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
About the size of a domestic chicken, these flightless New Zealand natives turn out to be more closely related to Madagascar's extinct elephant birds than to the giant moa — what are they?
Kiwi (bird) are flightless birds endemic to New Zealand of the order Apterygiformes.
A Ming-dynasty naturalist poured 27 years into a sprawling pharmacology compendium of nearly 1,900 entries, 11,000 prescriptions, and over a thousand herbs — who was this herbalist and physician?
Li Shizhen (July 3, 1518 - 1593), courtesy name Dongbi, was a Chinese acupuncturist, herbalist, naturalist, pharmacologist, physician, and writer of the Ming dynasty.
About 90% of its cases fall into the non-Hodgkin variety, and its tell-tale signs include painless swollen lymph nodes and night sweats — which group of white-blood-cell cancers is this?
Lymphoma is a group of blood and lymph tumors that develop from lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This dark-coated member of the weasel family comes in American and European species, plus an extinct 'sea' relative — what animal is it?

Mink are dark-coloured, semiaquatic, carnivorous mammals in the genera Mustela and Neogale and part of the family Mustelidae, which also includes weasels, stoats, martens, otters, badgers, and others.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Which Turkish-born American economist, an NYU Stern professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who predicted the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis?
Nouriel Roubini (born March 29, 1958) is a Turkish-born American economic consultant, economist, speaker, and writer.
Also called trioxygen and far less stable than the oxygen we breathe, it carries the formula O3 and smells faintly of chlorine — what is this gas?
Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3.
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity, wrapping most internal organs in a single sheet of mesothelium that also carries their blood vessels and nerves — what's the membrane?
Peritoneum is the serous membrane forming the lining of the abdominal cavity or coelom in amniotes and some invertebrates, such as annelids.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.

An Italian chemist and Auschwitz survivor, he wrote a celebrated memoir of his year in the camp and later a book of stories each named for a chemical element, hailed as the best science book ever — who was he?
Primo Levi (31 July 1919 - 11 April 1987) was a Jewish Italian chemist, partisan, Holocaust survivor and writer.
This Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian ever to travel to space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission in 1984 — who is he?
Rakesh Sharma (born 13 January 1949) is an Indian cosmonaut and a pilot of the Indian Air Force.
Named for its type genus, this plant family of nearly 4,800 species includes the trees and shrubs behind apples, pears, plums, cherries, and peaches — what family is it?
Rosaceae is a family of flowering plants that includes 4,828 known species in 91 genera.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
Holding the title of smallest great ape, this creature has pinker lips and a darker face than its close cousin, and was once dismissed as merely a 'pygmy' subspecies of it — what is it?
Bonobo: Species of great ape. Taxonomically, members of the chimpanzee/bonobo subtribe Panina—composed entirely by the genus Pan—are collectively termed panins.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Also known as Flinders rose, this perennial shrub with rounded fleshy leaves and white-to-pink flowers is native across circum-Mediterranean countries — what's the plant called?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This number-theory rule holds that if p is prime, then for any integer a, the value a to the power p minus a is always a multiple of p — which rule is this?

Fermat's little theorem: A prime p divides a^p–a for any integer a. Fermat's little theorem is the basis for the Fermat primality test and is one of the fundamental results of elementary number theory.
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
Brought to market by Monsanto in 1974 under the brand name Roundup, this herbicide works by blocking a key enzyme that plants need to grow — what is it?
Glyphosate: Systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
A founder of psychophysics, this German scientist captured how sensation relates to stimulus in a logarithmic law that now bears his and Weber's names — who was he?
Gustav Fechner: German experimental psychologist, physicist, and philosopher (1801–1887)

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?

When the thyroid produces too little hormone, the body slows down — cold intolerance, fatigue, constipation, weight gain — and worldwide too little dietary iodine is the leading cause. What's the condition?
Hypothyroidism: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
Known naturally as the mineral hematite, this reddish compound with formula Fe2O3 is the main source for the steel industry and gets reduced by aluminum in the fiery thermite reaction — what is it?
Iron(III) oxide: Chemical compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
This businessman and chemist owned the Lakers through their 1980s 'Showtime' era, winning 10 NBA titles before a Hall of Fame induction as a contributor — who was he?
Jerry Buss: American businessman and investor (1933–2013)
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
This sexually dimorphic East Asian perching waterfowl, closely related to North America's wood-dwelling cousin, gets its species name from a Latin word for a wig — which bird?
Mandarin duck: Species of bird. The mandarin duck (Aix galericulata) is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
Named from Greek words for 'small' and 'head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-average head size and can result from genetic syndromes or prenatal toxin exposure — what is it?
Microcephaly: Condition in which the head is small due to an underdeveloped brain.
Ranging from a tiny 8-inch species to the 10-foot Komodo dragon, this reptile genus includes an extinct relative that may have grown over 20 feet long — what are they called?
Monitor lizard: Genus of reptiles. Monitor lizards are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, this genus in the family Myrtaceae includes only two accepted species today: one native to the Mediterranean, the other to the Saharan mountains of North Africa — which genus?
Myrtus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
A former director of Russia's FSB who later served as Security Council secretary, this close Putin ally played a key role in the decisions to annex Crimea and invade Ukraine — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev: Russian politician and security officer (born 1951)

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
Whose name comes from Greek words for 'congealed' and 'curdled' — this plant-cell-wall polymer is extracted from citrus as a powder that makes jams and jellies set?
Pectin: Structural carbohydrate in the cell walls of land plants and some algae.
Grouped within the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, this genus contains today's living flamingo species — which genus?
This inflammatory lung condition attacks the tiny air sacs called alveoli, usually after a viral or bacterial infection, and often shows up on a chest X-ray — what is it?
Pneumonia: Inflammation of the alveoli of the lungs.
Discovered in 1857 by French chemist Marcellin Berthelot, this three-carbon alkane turns liquid under pressure and now fuels countless backyard barbecues — what gas is it?
A group of these mid-sized Galliformes birds is called a covey or bevy, and 40 million of them were farm-raised in the US back in 2007 alone — what bird is it?
Quail: Index of animals with the same common name.
Found in grape skins and produced by plants as a defense against injury or infection, this compound is touted as a longevity supplement despite scant evidence it helps — what is it?
Resveratrol: Polyphenol with a stilbene skeleton.
Operating under the alias 'Dread Pirate Roberts,' this American created and ran the dark-web marketplace Silk Road until his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht: American cybercriminal founder of Silk Road (born 1984)

Sometimes nicknamed the "seven-year itch," this contagious infestation by a tiny burrowing mite spreads fastest in crowded places and announces itself with fierce itching and a pimple-like rash — what is it?
This Pakistani-American billionaire owns an NFL franchise and a Premier League club, made his fortune supplying auto parts, and backs a wrestling promotion run by his son — who is he?
Shahid Khan: Pakistani and American businessman (born 1950)
Brittle, translucent, and found in nature as the mineral halite, this 1:1 compound seasons your fries and de-ices your roads. What is it?
Sodium chloride: Chemical compound with formula NaCl.
The most extreme form of malnutrition — a calorie deficit too deep to sustain life, sometimes wielded as a weapon and a crime under international law — goes by what name?
Starvation: Caloric intake below what is needed to maintain an organism's life.
Time named this marine biologist its first "Hero for the Planet" in 1998, the same year she became a National Geographic Explorer — and she'd already been NOAA's first chief scientist. Who is she?
Sylvia Earle: American marine biologist and lecturer.
Homologous to the ovary in females, this male gonad produces sperm and secretes testosterone under the control of the pituitary gland's luteinizing hormone — which organ?
Testicle: Internal organ in the male reproductive system.
Commonly called jock itch, this contagious fungal infection of the groin and buttocks causes an intensely itchy, red, scaly rash with a well-defined curved border — what is it?
Tinea cruris: Fungal infection. It is often associated with athlete's foot and fungal nail infections, excessive sweating, and sharing of infected towels or sports clothing.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.

Nicknamed the 'vampire fish' for feeding on the blood of larger fish through their gills, this tiny Amazonian catfish is infamous for an alleged, rare habit of entering human body openings — what is it?
Vandellia cirrhosa: Species of ray-finned fish.
